body:
Follow-up from the #646 sign-off (adversary review), accepted as a known limit in PR #648. Not fixed there.

**What happens.** `_finished_head` (`template/src/pdca_harness/flow.py:795-825` on `fix/646-stack-reissue-carries-clean-finished-prereqs`) judges each finished id on its own. Say a finished id `P` is not clean (for example, its PR was CLOSED), and a finished `Q` was built on `P` and is clean. Then `Q` is carried, and `P`'s commits come onto the line with it. `P`'s closed work leaks into the dependents through `Q`.

**Fix:** spread "not clean" along the edges. A finished id whose plain `Depends on` names a finished id that is not clean is itself not clean. Under #646's rule, that holds `Q`'s dependents too. Add a test with closed `P`, clean `Q` depending on `P`, and a dependent `D` of `Q`: `D` is held and the line has no commits from `P`.

Related: #624 (the hold of an unpublished bundle doesn't cascade through a pre-run COMPLETE dependent) is the same gap in a different place.

Source: `results/issue_646/SUMMARY.md` §10, `pr-description.md` "Known limits" (pdca-pdca).
title: stack mode: "not clean" does not cascade across finished ids — a closed P's commits ride onto the line through a clean Q built on it
